limitations: Native generation returned 1254×1254 rather than the requested 2048×2048. Normalized atlases repack native cutouts into larger transparent cells; they do not represent additional generated detail.
Direction views are separately rendered illustrations, not guaranteed renders of one rigid 3D model. Small panel, ridge, and joint differences remain between views.
Bristleback ridge counts vary slightly across views, matching the reference’s ridged silhouette. The gameplay identity remains the red six-legged creature.
Ground anchor uses the lowest visible contact edge at y=338. Unit and loose-part bounds are centered horizontally; trees, flag and relay center their lower physical base at x=192.
execution_order: Isolate alpha islands and normalize individual cells
Repack uniform atlases and embed exact generation prompts
Inspect full atlases plus game-size and roster-size previews
assumptions: Original glossy toy materials and approved saturated palette are binding.
The same individual PNG textures supply game units and larger roster/blueprint imagery.
No new art direction or full background scene is introduced.

All object frames at 80px cell size
Four southeast roster views at 256px cell size
visual_review.findings: All subjects fit their cells and match the approved glossy toy vocabulary. Front and rear views read distinctly; Hauler beds are empty; alpha cutouts contain no text, floor or baked shadows. Native detached edge specks removed.

source_atlases.note: Normalized cutouts; runtime uses individual pictures.

rendering.sourceAlignment: Lowest visible edge at y338 is export padding alignment, not a physical footprint center.
rendering.occlusion: World footprint y; carried parts are children of their carrier.
rendering.shadows: Soft contact graphics on a shared ground layer below all upright objects.
rendering.markers: Ground-space marks below objects; status above them. Loose-part count badges appear only on hover.
rendering.terrain: Water below raised terrain; each land or bridge tile paints its faces, top and outline together, back to front.
rendering.facing: src/view/facing.ts corrects rear-view exports: ne pictures face northwest, and nw pictures face northeast.
